gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the maker-declared SSD exclusions differ by enclosure: UGREEN's fan model (SKU 45789) excludes all PCIe 5.0 SSDs including the Samsung 9100 and has no USB 2/3 fallback (Thunderbolt 3 only on macOS 15+), while OWC's Express 1M2 80G allows Gen 5 drives only if they average 11 W or less and ACASIS's current TB501 Pro/Max claims native Gen 5 support and recommends the 9100 Pro.
standout_why: Compared against the cited ACASIS product pages (one was rate-limited; the Shopify data for the other was read), DPReview's roundup and OWC's buying guide. ChatGPT's answer says only that the '$149 basic' ACASIS lacks PCIe 5.0 and that newer ones have it; DPReview gives no SSD or cable pairing rules; OWC's blog says nothing about Gen 5 power limits, drive sizes or fallback modes. None of them states UGREEN's Gen 5 / Samsung 9100 exclusion, the no-USB-3-fallback limit, OWC's 11 W Gen 5 ceiling, or Apple's own cable spec (1 m passive, 120 Gb/s on TB5, 80 Gb/s on TB4/USB4, 240 W). Apple's support page confirming base M4 = Thunderbolt 4 and M4 Pro/Max = Thunderbolt 5 is already stated by ChatGPT, so that part is not new.
decides: It confirms ChatGPT's pairing of a PCIe 4.0 Samsung 990 Pro with any of the three enclosures, but adds the decisive exclusions a shopper hits if they already own or plan a Gen 5 drive: with the UGREEN fan model it is unsupported by the maker, with the OWC it must average 11 W or less (OWC names the 9100 Pro as a passing example), and ACASIS is the only one of the three that claims unrestricted native Gen 5 support. It also narrows the pick for anyone who needs to plug the drive into a plain USB 3 port (older Mac, dock, PC): UGREEN says its fan enclosure is not backward compatible with USB 2/3, whereas our page already notes ORICO's X50 Pro and UGREEN's finned model carry a USB fallback controller. Base-M4 buyers get Thunderbolt 4 ports only, so OWC's own figure of up to 3,800 MB/s applies and the TB5 premium is wasted.
